IS IT A FREQUENCY?

No single one. The songs’ home notes are spread across the octave, and their tuning varies too.
◉

These are measurements of recordings, not of your brain. Automatic chord and key estimates make mistakes, especially with Indian melodic modes and old recordings. No song or setting here is a migraine treatment. Your audio never leaves this browser, and Still stores no audio.

03 · CHORD ROLES

How the chords are used

Share of chord time in each role relative to the song’s home key. Lower case means a minor chord. In A minor, i = Am, ♭VII = G, ♭VI = F and V = E. Even the best trained key finders get about 68–80% of pop songs exactly right, and simpler methods on old film recordings likely do worse; errors are usually a fifth away or the relative major/minor.

04 · SCALE NOTES

Which notes they lean on

Average energy on each note of the scale, measured from the home note, for major-key songs (gold) and minor-key songs (green) separately. Overtones blur this picture: every note also lights up its fifth and major third a little.

    Is this what you like?

    The zone describes your songs; it is not a brain measurement. Whether it is what calms you is a hypothesis. To check it, play a sketch, then “Hear the other version”: the same notes, matched to the zone or plain, at the same loudness. Rate both, and Still keeps score of these pairs.

    08 · YOUR SONG MAP

    Every song as a vector

    SIMILARITY SEARCH, NOT HIT PREDICTION

    Each song becomes a vector built from what Song DNA measures: scale-note use, chord roles, tempo, harmony rhythm, repetition, frequency shape and a little production. Songs that sound alike sit close together. The map flattens those vectors to two dimensions, so it shows only part of the picture.

        Automatic triad labels over ~0.4 s windows, shown only for a song you analyse here and never stored. Sevenths, suspended chords and raga phrases are forced onto the nearest major or minor triad. Expert listeners themselves agree on chord roots only about 76–94% of the time.

        10 · MAKE A STYLE SKETCH

        An original sketch in this style

        NO MELODY IS COPIED

        Pick a progression, key, tempo and feel. It plays at your comfort-profile level for your current state (or your quiet reference if you have no profile), fades in slowly, and the level slider only goes quieter. Still builds a new instrumental from those ingredients, with a melody made from random chord tones. Chord progressions, keys and tempos are shared musical building blocks; no song’s melody or recording is used.

        How did it feel?

        HOW THIS WORKS, AND ITS LIMITS

        Same analyser everywhere

        The profile and your comparisons use the same code (song-dna.js). It was checked on synthetic songs with known keys, chords, tempos and tuning, and cross-checked against librosa on the real recordings.

        What it can’t see

        Lyrics, the singer’s voice, memories and the films these songs belong to. Familiar music engages the brain’s reward regions more than liking alone, and nostalgia is likely a big part of why these songs feel peaceful to you. No spectrum can measure that.

        Popular is not the same as typical

        These songs are all famous, so the profile shows what they share, not what made them hits. Studies of tens of thousands of songs found audio features predict popularity poorly; film, lyrics, radio play and stardom dominate.

        Your taste decides

        Rate sketches as you listen. Over time Still can learn which progressions, tempos and textures calm you, the same way your comfort profile learns which sounds feel gentle.
